hypotheses.claim: A direct hook that separates one bad Virgo ex from the whole sign will create more recognition and debate than repeating a generic Virgo dating stereotype.
hypotheses.success_metric: 7d completion_rate >= 0.35 and comments explicitly agree, disagree, or share a counterexample about judging a sign from one ex

hypotheses.claim: A same-sign, different-treatment contrast will make the non-deterministic message more concrete than an abstract reminder that behavior is not destiny.
hypotheses.success_metric: 7d completion_rate >= 0.35 and comments explicitly recognize or challenge the same-sign-different-treatment contrast

backlog.title: Your Virgo Ex Is Not Evidence About Every Virgo
backlog.hook: One bad Virgo ex does not prove every Virgo will treat you the same way.
backlog.angle: Virgo | Single AI host | Start with the temptation to turn one painful relationship into a sign-wide rule, then contrast it with a recent community counterexample describing steady care. Keep both examples as anecdotes, not astrology facts, and end on the behavior the viewer should actually watch.

backlog.title: Same Virgo Sign, Completely Different Partner
backlog.hook: Two Virgos can share the same sign and treat you completely differently.
backlog.angle: Virgo | Single AI host | Use two opposite lived examples from the same discussion—steady practical care versus harmful behavior—to show that a sign can frame a pattern but cannot predict a person's choices. Keep the focus on observable treatment, not compatibility scores or diagnosis.
backlog.why_now: checked_at=2026-08-18; research topic miraa-w34-test-t05 is supported by verified source src-4b653b6b36, whose readable thread contains kindness, harm, and ordinary incompatibility in the same sign discussion. Dedupe: not the existing Virgo acts-of-care candidate; the single test variable is same sign versus different treatment. Evidence remains single-platform and qualitative.
backlog.route_reason: Evergreen Route C. One AI host can explain the contrast clearly while preserving the current production baseline and avoiding a deterministic claim. P1 test; S effort; H3 selection required.
